rule: Divider lines split the grid into regions. In a region holding a corner-anchored diagonal chain of cells (read from the corner inward, a leading background cell allowed), every cell gets chain[(ring-1) % len]. The ring is the Chebyshev distance to outside the region. The divider and seedless regions are unchanged.
scope: Supported: random sizes 10..30 per side; random background and divider colours; guillotine line splits (T-junctions); hollow boxes, floating or flush with walls or corners, giving annular and L-shaped regions; chains of 1-4 distinct colours, optionally led by one background cell, at any convex corner and any of four diagonal directions; regions left empty as distractors. Not supported: diagonal or thick dividers, background cells inside a chain other than in the leading position, more than one chain per region.
constraints: Divider lines are 1-thick, axis-aligned, and in a single colour different from the background.
The background is strictly the most frequent input colour.
Coloured chain entries are distinct and exclude divider/background. One optional leading background entry is allowed; the last entry is non-background.
Chain cell i lies at ring distance i+1, so the chain matches the ring structure.
Every maximal-count corner-anchored diagonal reading of the region's seeds equals the intended chain, so there is no ambiguous alternative corner.
At least two regions and at least one chain exist, and the output differs from the input.
known_limitations: Layouts are limited to guillotine splits plus hollow boxes. Arbitrary partial line networks like every possible ARC layout are not sampled.
Chain length is capped at 4 coloured cells plus one optional leading background cell.
Random dimensions must be 10..30; 300 failed construction attempts raise explicitly without a canned fallback.
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback
